note: The exact questions a record answers, in this order, with pass, fail or not_run. A record must answer every question of its platform's list; there is no way to add, drop or reorder one. Guided platforms answer `assertions` through the recorder; automated platforms answer `automatedAssertions` from Playwright test annotations (@assertion:<id>) run against the candidate URL. WebKit automation is its own platform and never stands in for either Safari; a desktop browser never stands in for a phone.

assertions.text: The page loads over HTTPS with no certificate warning, on a certificate this platform trusts.
The owner signs in, creates an invite, and a new member joins with it.
A member signs in with a password; a wrong password is refused.
A chat message sends, shows for a second browser and survives a reload; a mention reaches its recipient.
HLS video plays and seeks.
Direct audio plays and seeks.
An EPUB opens, paginates and keeps its place, and a PDF opens.
A multi-track audiobook plays and carries on across tracks.
A file uploads, downloads byte-identical and deletes.
Commentary can be written, shared, replied to and removed.
Settings opens, and an administrator manages members, invites and roles.
Signing out ends the session and signing back in works.
With Jellyfin stopped only Stream degrades, with Grimmory stopped only Library degrades, and both recover.
With the network dropped the app shows its offline state and reconnects without a reload.
Keyboard-only navigation reaches every control with visible focus, the layout works at phone and desktop widths, and text zooms to 200% without loss.

automatedAssertions.text: The origin is HTTPS on a certificate the browser trusts and the page comes from the static client.
The owner signs in, creates an invite, and a new member joins with it.
A member signs in with a password; a wrong password is refused.
A chat message sends and survives a reload.
A file uploads, downloads byte-identical and deletes.
Commentary can be written on a file.
Stream and Library show real content or their own unavailable state.
Settings opens, and an administrator reaches the administration sections.
Signing out ends the session and signing back in works.
With Jellyfin stopped only Stream degrades, with Grimmory stopped only Library degrades, and both recover.
With the network dropped the app shows its offline state and reconnects without a reload.
The shell lays out at phone and desktop widths with every module reachable.

linux-appimage.name: Telos AppImage on Ubuntu Linux x86-64

assertions.text: The exact AppImage is installed and its SHA-256 equals the identity sidecar's.
Connecting to a node with an untrusted certificate is refused with no override.
Connecting to the trusted HTTPS node shows no certificate prompt.
Signing in works and the device appears in Settings, Devices in the hosted browser.
Chat, Stream, Library and Files open; covers and avatars render; an ebook reads.
HLS video, direct audio and a multi-track audiobook play and seek (record whether native HLS or hls.js played).
Commentary can be created and read.
After quitting fully and relaunching, the user is signed in without typing the password.
Past the access-token lifetime with chat and playback active, nothing drops and no second device appears.
Revoking the device in the browser makes the next request, media segment and socket fail.
After signing out, quitting and relaunching, no credential remains in the keyring.
